topic: Module A: Language, Identity and Culture
prompt: Read the extract: “My father spoke two languages: one for the shop and one for the kitchen. In the shop he said Sir and Thank you and Have a good day. In the kitchen he sang, he swore, he told stories about a river I had never seen. I learned early which father I preferred, and later, which one had kept us fed.” Analyse how the extract represents the ways language shapes identity and belonging.
stmt_text: Read the extract: “My father spoke two languages: one for the shop and one for the kitchen. In the shop he said Sir and Thank you and Have a good day. In the kitchen he sang, he swore, he told stories about a river I had never seen. I learned early which father I preferred, and later, which one had kept us fed.” Analyse how the extract represents the ways language shapes identity and belonging.
sol_text:
Model answer:
Thesis: language divides the father's identity into a public, assimilated self and a private, cultural self, and the child comes to see the value of both.
Contrast and repetition ("one for the shop and one for the kitchen") structure the split identity.
Listing of polite formulas ("Sir and Thank you and Have a good day") shows a restricted, performed identity, while the energetic verbs "sang, he swore, he told" show freedom and authenticity.
"a river I had never seen" shows inherited cultural memory the child belongs to only through language.
The final sentence's parallel structure ("which father I preferred ... which one had kept us fed") shows mature recognition of the sacrifice of adopting a new language.

- General or limited response (1 mark)
Equivalent methods and wording that show the same understanding get the same marks.
